title: PDF / Office to Markdown
goal: Turn PDFs, Office files, HTML, ZIP files, and other documents into Markdown that AI agents can read, summarize, and transform.

primary_tools.name: MarkItDown
primary_tools.role: Broad document-to-Markdown conversion for LLM and text-analysis pipelines

when_to_use: You need a quick Markdown version of PDFs, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, ZIP, YouTube, or EPUB content.
You want portfolio, research, or product documents in a format Codex and other agents can inspect.
You care more about useful semantic text than pixel-perfect layout preservation.
when_not_to_use: You need reliable layout coordinates, citation highlights, or complex table reconstruction.
The document is sensitive and you have not reviewed the local tool's security behavior.
You need a high-fidelity human-facing conversion.

demo.notes: No third-party tool is executed. This fixture demonstrates the desired Markdown shape for a safe document-conversion workflow.

codex_prompt: Use the document-to-Markdown capability to convert the supplied document into Markdown for AI review. Preserve headings, lists, tables, links, and key metadata where possible. Mark uncertain tables or OCR-sensitive sections for manual review. Do not invent missing content.
verification: Document headings and lists are preserved when present.
Tables are either preserved or explicitly marked as uncertain.
The result is suitable for summarization, feature-spec extraction, or portfolio cleanup.
risks: Document converters run with the privileges of the current process; avoid untrusted or sensitive files until the runner design is reviewed.
Markdown output may be good for LLM ingestion but not high-fidelity enough for human-facing layout.
